findings.reason: The former 'within each grain' claim is replaced by slip that can occur inside individual grains. The next short paragraph explicitly says it need not begin in all grains at once and that some grains can remain elastic while others slip. This removes universal participation as well as simultaneous onset. Different easy-slip planes/directions and the qualified polycrystal comparison remain.
findings.sourceMeaning: Slip within individual small crystals is retained without attributing obligatory all-grain participation to the source.

findings.reason: Atoms, elements, crystal, deformation, load and strain now receive plain local explanations. Equilibrium positions are identified as usual average positions, and the next paragraph expressly retains microscopic motion around them. Elastic recovery is explained through removing a push or pull; approximate atomic recovery remains conditional on no damage or irreversible change, which is immediately explained. The permanent-change contrast remains. Seven two-sentence paragraphs give the strong eight-year-old reader manageable steps; the elastic-range meaning follows nearby without a missing causal link.
findings.sourceMeaning: Small elastic displacement and changes in particle spacing/arrangement remain, without turning recovery into microscopic immobility or a guarantee after irreversible damage.

findings.reason: Lattice and a flat crystal plane are explained before slip; single crystal and tension are explained before their figure context. Force per unit area leads to neighboring parts sliding, then to the name shear and suitable planes/directions. The dislocation explanation now connects an imperfect line in the repeating arrangement to nearby particles rearranging in small steps and a lasting relative shift. The simplified-result model still denies necessary simultaneous rigid movement of complete layers. Short definition and causal paragraphs support independent reading; the longer qualification paragraph has concrete previously introduced referents.
findings.sourceMeaning: Accumulated relative shifts, retained order under slip without fracture or structural transformation, and the distinction from unchanged neighbors or a perfect lattice are preserved. Panel a remains associated with surface slip marks under tension; panel b remains a simplified offset after slip. These are text-context conclusions only.

findings.reason: Orientation now means which way the repeating pattern faces; grain boundary means where grains meet; fitting against neighbors provides the accommodation link. Boundary hindrance leads explicitly to more stress before permanent deformation, and 'this extra stress' has a clear referent. Smaller grains explain fine-grained material. The comparison is tied to suitable slip conditions for the material with comparable temperature/loading, and the arbitrary-single-crystal-orientation exception remains explicit. The closing list translates composition, pattern directions and loading into ordinary language. Two- or three-sentence paragraphs keep the comparison and its limits readable.
findings.sourceMeaning: The source's differing slip directions, possible higher starting stress and fine-grain observation remain qualified, not a universal material ranking. Completely random orientations and grain-size-only judgments are not asserted.

affectedScience.reason: No all-grain requirement, universal slip mechanism, rigid simultaneous-layer requirement, unconditional recovery, perfect-lattice claim or universal polycrystal ranking was introduced. Slip/dislocation mechanisms and their conditions remain.
